title: Prefill Orbit Tuner: phase-aware kernel hedging with sequence-length forecasting
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: We see intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes (~30-60ms additional) on mixed short/long sequence workloads when the runtime picks a single kernel per model without accounting for phase (prefill vs decode) and short-term sequence-length distribution. Goal: Build a lightweight "orbit" tuner that forecasts per-workload sequence-length distribution and performs phase-aware kernel hedging (prefer small-latency kernels for short prefill bursts, switch to throughput-friendly kernels as decode grows) with conservative rollback to avoid quality regressions. The tuner should run with minimal per-request overhead, leverage microbenchmarks, and respect per-tenant constraints (Dedicated vs Hosted).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Implement the orbit tuner that selects kernels independently for prefill and decode phases using a lightweight seqlen forecast.
2) End-to-end A/B shows >=8% reduction in p95 latency for mixed short/long traffic buckets without >2% regression in mean token throughput.
3) Cost model estimates show <=3% increase in GPU-hours for the improvement in tail latency (or net cost reduction when batching gains applied).
4) Feature flags and rollout policy exist: canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) and immediate rollback.
5) Documentation: design doc + runbook + perf dashboard published.
experiment_plan:
Phase A - Offline microbench: run kernels (attn-tiling, fused-attn, sparse variant, small-kernel low-latency) across A100/H100/AMD with seqlen buckets [<=16,17-64,65-256,>256] and batch sizes [1,4,16]. Collect cost/latency/throughput profiles.
Phase B - Canary: enable orbit tuner for 5% of Hosted traffic with A/B control; monitor p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, model output diffs on eval prompts, and GPU utilization.
Phase C - Scale: 25% for 48h, then assess. Success threshold: per-bucket p95 reduced by >=8% and no eval regression flagged by quality monitors.
Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-1M-tokens, rollback events, model output divergence rate (syntactic and semantic thresholds).
implementation_notes:
Algorithm sketch: 1) Maintain lightweight per-route rolling histogram of observed input sequence lengths (TTL=10m); 2) Forecast next-window distribution via exponential smoothing + simple weekday/hour adjustment; 3) For an incoming request, pick prefill kernel using short-tail-penalized cost model and select decode kernel with throughput-weighted objective; 4) If sequence-length is unknown (cold-start), run microprobe: 1-2 sample runs on candidate kernels (prefill microprobe on first 2 requests only) with strict time budget and prefer cached warmstarts; 5) Use temporal hedging for first N tokens (orbit window) to keep p95 low and then switch to throughput kernel.
Engineering constraints: no additional GPU-side agents — decision must be made in the runtime scheduler. Kernel switch must preserve KV cache compatibility or rehydrate cache gracefully. Quantization and mixed-precision compatibility must be validated per kernel pair.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Microprobes add startup overhead; mitigate by limiting probes to 1-2 requests and caching results per route.
Frequent kernel switches may thrash caches and increase latency; limit switch frequency and require minimum session duration before switching back.
Heterogeneous hardware means a kernel that is good on H100 might be poor on AMD; require per-arch profiling and store profiles separately.
Quality risk if a kernel variant changes numerics; include evaluation harness and model output diff thresholds before rollouts.
notes: 2025-01-16: Spike complete — validated that fused-attn is fastest for decode on long sequences for Genoa models, but small-kernel tiling wins prefill for short sequences on A100.
2025-01-20: UX/Console integration: added a toggle to show per-route orbit decisions in runtime traces (PR #4921).
2025-01-29: PM review (Markus Chen) — asked for a conservative rollout and explicit cost accounting per tenant. Added cost threshold guardrails.
2025-02-02: Design review — agreed on TTL=10m for seqlen histograms and 1-2 microprobes for cold start.
rollout_plan: Start with Hosted routes labeled 'experimental' via feature flag. Canary window: 5% traffic x 24h, monitor rollback triggers (p95 increase >5% or eval divergence >0.5%). If stable -> 25% x 48h -> 100% with staggered tenant-by-tenant migration for Dedicated. Provide immediate kill switch for control plane.
rollback_plan: Disable feature flag; runtime reverts to baseline kernel selection. Ensure a fast GC of per-route microprobe caches to avoid stale decisions. Postmortem: collect last 48h traces and microprobe logs, run offline repro on dedicated bench cluster.
qa_checks: 1) Unit tests for forecast logic and histogram TTL. 2) Integration tests on simulator with synthetic seqlen distributions. 3) Perf regression tests against baseline using 10k synthetic sessions per GPU type. 4) Eval run to compare model outputs on canonical prompt set.
owner_notes: Next steps: land profiler adapters for AMD, complete PR #4921 code review, and schedule canary for 2025-02-05. If canary fails, fallback to single-kernel policy with annotated reason codes.
